findings.problem: With no hint, "candy" could just as well be "el caramelo" or "la golosina", both common in much of Latin America (e.g., Argentina, Peru, Venezuela), so el dulce isn't the only right answer.
findings.fix: hint: the noun form of the word for "sweet"

back.es: candy, sweet (a piece of candy); also a sweet dessert or preserve
back.example: Will you give me a candy?

note: In Spain, "caramelo" means a hard candy specifically, and "golosina" or "chuche" is the general word, so "caramelo" is an acceptable Spain alternative but a narrow one.
